name: Emily Randall

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: FEDERAL PROGRAM INTEGRITY AND FRAUD PREVENTION ACT OF 2026
statements.title: FEDERAL PROGRAM INTEGRITY AND FRAUD PREVENTION ACT OF 2026
sentences: Mr. Speaker, I rise today in support of the Federal Program Integrity and Fraud Prevention Act, bipartisan legislation that I am proud to lead with Representative Self.
Mr. Speaker, I urge all my colleagues to support the Federal Program Integrity and Fraud Prevention Act.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: TESTIMONY OF MS. COURTNEY WILD, "SURVIVORS FIGHT FOR JUSTICE: EXPOSING EPSTEIN'S CRIMES IN PALM BEACH AND ACROSS THE WORLD"
statements.title: TESTIMONY OF MS. COURTNEY WILD, "SURVIVORS FIGHT FOR JUSTICE: EXPOSING EPSTEIN'S CRIMES IN PALM BEACH AND ACROSS THE WORLD"
sentences: Mr. Speaker on May 12, 2026, Oversight Committee Democrats convened the first-ever hearing to solicit testimony from survivors of Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell's crimes.
The hearing, ``Survivors Fight for Justice: Exposing Epstein's Crimes in Palm Beach and Across the World,'' marked a critical step forward in the fight for justice and accountability.
On behalf of all the survivors of Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell's crimes, I rise to include in the Record the testimony offered by Ms. Courtney Wild: Hello.
When I was 14 years old, I was abused by Jeffrey Epstein.
I filed a case under the Crime Victims' Rights Act because the government secretly made a deal with Jeffrey Epstein.

We had to fight all the way to the Eleventh Circuit, which took years, just to get the emails between the government and Jeffrey's lawyers to help us understand what happened, When we finally got them, they showed something I will never forget-- The government wasn't just negotiating with Epstein's lawyers, it looked like the government was trying to make him happy and make sure that he was okay with the punishment that they were going to give him.

But the point is that Jeffrey Epstein continued to abuse other girls in New York, in New Mexico, around the world, and even still here in Florida after he was released in 2009 and everyone knew it, There were lawsuits.
Jeffrey Epstein should have been in jail.
If the point is to figure out who helped Jeffrey Epstein commit his crimes--then look at the professionals that were in his life.
We fought for years to have Jeffrey Epstein arrested.
So, I am asking you to fix that.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PREGNANT STUDENTS' RIGHTS ACT
statements.title: PREGNANT STUDENTS' RIGHTS ACT
sentences: It has decimated Medicaid, the number one payer for births in this country, in order to pay for tax breaks for the ultrawealthy and fund ICE's violent reign in our communities.

If we believed in supporting student parents, we would put more money into childcare subsidies, more money into financial aid, and more money into food assistance so that the women in college, the people who are students who get pregnant, who have a tough decision to make, would have all of the resources and support they need to make the decision that is right for them.

I have had a chance to work with a lot of students who have become pregnant, both from around the time I was in junior high, when a friend of mine had a pregnancy scare, to a time when I was in college, to being a volunteer in the bay area where I was on a rapid response line in case someone needed to take a bus 3\1/2\ hours from their college campus into the city.
That is because that was the only place they could access either maternity care, OB/GYN care, or access abortion care.
Mr. Speaker, I rise today in strong opposition to H.R. 6359, a bill that claims to protect pregnant students but actually mandates that they get less, not more information about their rights.
Mr. Speaker, I urge all of my colleagues to vote ``no'' on this bill and to take serious action to support students, pregnant or not.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROTECTING HEALTHCARE FOR MILLIONS OF AMERICANS
statements.title: PROTECTING HEALTHCARE FOR MILLIONS OF AMERICANS
sentences: Across our country, working families are feeling the pain of rising costs from every direction.
Now, Republican leadership, who love to extend tax breaks for billionaires, are making things worse by, for months, refusing to extend the Affordable Care Act's tax credits for regular people.
They were created because the U.S. has the most expensive healthcare system in the world, and without help, millions of working families are simply unable to afford coverage.
Right now, families who rely on the ACA in Washington's Sixth are facing an average increase of $1,500 a month in healthcare costs.

This Republican-created crisis will price out an estimated 80,000 Washingtonians from coverage, and that doesn't even include the millions more in Washington and across the country who are losing care because of the cuts to Medicaid and Medicare.
Women who are already struggling with restrictions to reproductive care, who make less money than men do, and who are on the front lines of growing childcare crises.

LGBTQ Americans, who are more likely to rely on the ACA because of lower incomes and employment discrimination, on top of this administration rapidly stripping away access to their lifesaving care and protections.
Families really struggling to get by, living paycheck to paycheck, are more likely to work jobs without employer-provided benefits, making the ACA their only real option for coverage.
I want to make this clear: Republican leadership let tax credits expire in order to pay for tax breaks for billionaires.

That is why, in the State legislature, I worked every day to protect and expand access to care, passing laws to expand postpartum Medicaid so that new parents received the care that they needed after childbirth, establishing a universal healthcare commission, removing barriers to behavioral health and dental care, and lowering prescription drug prices.
While families are worried about whether they can afford insulin, inhalers, or mental health care, Republican leadership chose inaction.
I am very glad that 17 of my Republican colleagues joined Democrats today in doing the right thing by voting to extend the ACA tax credits for 3 more years to protect access to affordable healthcare.

We need a system where no one lies awake at night wondering if they will be able to afford insulin, whether they will be able to afford it if their kid breaks their arm, or whether they will be able to afford it if their spouse has a pregnancy complication or a cancer diagnosis.
The United States, arguably the wealthiest country in the world, doesn't have a universal healthcare system like every advanced nation in the world does.
Amanda in Bremerton told us that for her family, the ACA credits were the only way that she could afford healthcare.
If they lose the discount with the ACA, they wouldn't be able to have healthcare, period.

The insurance that they offer would cost her $1,000 a month, which is out of her budget, but obtaining insurance through the Washington marketplace, with ACA tax credits, allowed her to purchase it for just $300 a month, less than a third of what her employer-sponsored coverage would be.
She makes just too much money to receive Apple Health, our version of Medicaid.
She will be swimming in medical debt.

Our neighbors deserve better, and they deserve us to keep fighting, not just for this ACA tax credit extension, which we will continue to put pressure on the Senate to pass, but also for a system that meets our needs nationwide.
By refusing to extend the Affordable Care Act tax credits before they expired last month, they made healthcare costs more expensive for working families when people are already stretched thin.
If the Senate doesn't pass the 3-year ACA extension immediately, families will be locked into these higher prices for 2026, and they will lose coverage.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: STANDARDIZING PERMITTING AND EXPEDITING ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT ACT
statements.title: STANDARDIZING PERMITTING AND EXPEDITING ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT ACT
sentences: Yes, we need more transmission and clean energy projects, and it is true that the permitting process is making that more difficult.

They have fired Federal workers and illegally canceled funding Congress already approved, including over $1 billion for clean energy projects in Washington State that had strong community support: a long-anticipated hydrogen hub in the south sound, solar projects across the State and the country, and freight and drayage improvements in the trucking industry that would lower the cost of goods and decrease our environmental impact.

That is why I offered two amendments: one, to give Tribes sufficient time to engage in the permitting process, and then another to ensure the offshore oil and gas drilling projects, rubber-stamped by H.R. 1, July's big, ugly law, still have to consider community feedback.
Republicans blocked my amendments, which is why I am voting ``no'' on the SPEED Act, a bill that doesn't address the challenges my neighbors are experiencing.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PET AND LIVESTOCK PROTECTION ACT
statements.title: PET AND LIVESTOCK PROTECTION ACT
sentences: The kids and parents in my community live their lives in terror, and they have it the best, because Washington State is a place where we have fought to protect healthcare access for LGBTQ kids and trans kids.
This effort not only to cut Medicaid coverage but to try to ban access for children-- Mr. Speaker, this behavior is appalling.
I spend a lot of time in LGBTQ clubs in high schools, talking to young people who are shocked when I come in and tell them that, as a queer woman, I am a Member of Congress.

Mr. Speaker, I have been sitting here listening to the remarks on the floor, and I have to admit that I find myself torn between heartbroken tears and the urge to throw something, which I will not do because I am a professional human being.
Mr. Speaker, I think it is very clear that I am not going to vote for this bill, and I urge all of my colleagues to join me.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: QUINAULT INDIAN NATION LAND TRANSFER ACT
statements.title: QUINAULT INDIAN NATION LAND TRANSFER ACT
sentences: I rise today in strong support of this bill, the Quinault Indian Nation Land Transfer Act, and I thank Chairman Westerman and Indian and Insular Affairs Subcommittee Chairman Hurd for the opportunity to speak about another bill before us today and for their thoughtful engagement with Tribal council members, Tribal President Capoeman, when he came before the committee, and Quinault Business Committee member Tyson Johnston, who testified to the importance of this legislation earlier this year.
Earlier this year, I reintroduced the Quinault Indian Nation Land Transfer Act in partnership with Senators Cantwell and Murray.
This bill would return approximately 72 acres of land, as we have heard, known as Allotment 1157, to the Quinault Indian Nation by placing it into trust with the Department of the Interior.
I am proud to champion this bill, and I urge my colleagues to support its passage.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: REPUBLICAN HEALTHCARE CRISIS
statements.title: REPUBLICAN HEALTHCARE CRISIS
sentences: At the end of the month, the Affordable Care Act enhanced premium tax credits will officially expire, leaving 24 million Americans who currently purchase healthcare on the exchange in an unimaginable position.

Even with insurance provided by my dad's civilian job at the Department of Defense, Olivia wouldn't have gotten the care that she needed to live for 19 years as healthy as possible if it weren't for the Washington State Legislature expanding Medicaid the year she was born.
My family would have faced dire choices about which bills not to pay in order to meet Olivia's needs if it weren't for Medicaid access.

We have now determined that the best way to cover our upcoming healthcare costs will be for me to take my Social Security early.'' She says: ``It is upsetting to me that my Social Security will not be used for other living expenses or be as much per month as it would have if I could hold off taking it a few more years.'' She is worried in her last line about not being able to use her Social Security for other living expenses because she is going to have to use all of it for healthcare coverage.

It is time for my colleagues to get serious about solving the ACA tax credits, as serious as they were about extending tax breaks for billionaires in July, and get back to delivering on their promise to lower costs for Americans, which Trump promised to do on day one of his administration. ____________________

I recently heard from a neighbor in Port Townsend who said: ``My husband is retiring in a few weeks.'' She retired years ago. ``So although we currently have a good benefits package through his work, we will be on our own for coverage soon.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PRESERVING RURAL HEALTHCARE ACCESS IS LITERALLY LIFE AND DEATH
statements.title: PRESERVING RURAL HEALTHCARE ACCESS IS LITERALLY LIFE AND DEATH
sentences: At Grays Harbor Community Hospital, I saw firsthand how tariffs are driving up costs for medical devices and supplies, adding financial strain to already stretched rural facilities.

The hospital recently invested in a new MRI machine, a critical upgrade that offers faster scans and higher resolution images, but because of tariffs, they had to pay significantly more money to purchase this machine.
Add to that the Medicaid cuts in the big, ugly bill and the end of the ACA tax credits, the strain and uncertainty is challenging.

It is telling people that your health and your lives aren't worth as much as billionaires' bank accounts. ____________________

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: REPUBLICAN BUDGET BETRAYAL
statements.title: REPUBLICAN BUDGET BETRAYAL
sentences: However, gratefully for our family, the Washington State legislature in 1993 voted to expand Medicaid.

So for the last 6 years in the Washington State legislature I worked hard to expand healthcare access for folks all across the State and all across my big rural district where hospitals are already struggling because Medicaid reimbursement rates are low, where small clinics and independent providers are shuttering their doors because they cannot afford to stay open.

We should not be adding to it by cutting $1 trillion from poor people and people with disabilities, from children, and from seniors who are often dual eligible for Medicare and Medicaid who are able to live in dignity until the end of their days because of this important program.
It will keep long-term care programs open if we are able to maintain Medicaid funding.
I am also scared for the impact that we will see for years into the future if this budget resolution becomes law, if we deliver trillions of dollars of cuts for families who depend on Medicaid.
What will happen if this budget resolution becomes reality and if $1 trillion is cut from Medicare programs is that we will see potentially per-capita caps.
What that means is that we will decide how much the lives of children like my sister are worth.

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND GIRLS IN SPORTS ACT OF 2025
statements.title: PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND GIRLS IN SPORTS ACT OF 2025
sentences: It gives every teacher, coach, and parent an opportunity to police who looks feminine enough to play.
As LGBTQ+ youth continue to face attacks and targeting from extremist lawmakers in legislative chambers across the country and higher rates of depression and suicide, this bill is doubly dangerous.
Mr. Speaker, I urge all of my colleagues to focus on addressing the pressing issues facing everyday Americans and to reject this hateful legislation.
